messages:
Alice: thinking out loud — we need a single decision graph that maps (tenant tier, region, realtime load, quota state) -> route + fallback strategy. current ad-hoc rules are getting messy and the console UX can't show why a request hit a cheap variant.
Ben: agree. can you sketch the nodes? is this purely priority weights or a stateful FSM?
Alice: sketch attached (will paste inline). idea: 1) check hard quota breach -> block or rate-limit; 2) check soft quota -> prefer cheaper variants with graceful degrade; 3) check latency SLO -> prefer regional low-latency replicas; 4) fallback chain if capacity shortage. each node outputs telemetry tags so UI can explain.
Carole: quick question on hard vs soft quotas — do we enforce soft quotas client-side (reject) or just bias routing? my vote: soft = bias only, hard = reject/failover to billing path.
Ben: +1 to Carole. also want a per-tenant "grace budget" that can be consumed for short bursts (tracked separately).
Maria: from telemetry POV we need these fields on every request: tenant_id, tier, quota_state (normal/soft/hard), route_decision (primary_variant/fallback_chain), decision_reason, latency_target, token_cost_estimate. dashboards should let us filter by decision_reason and see failover rates over time.
Dave: API shape proposal — a single policy blob per tenant with three sections: tier_policies, route_pools, fallback_matrix. small example:
```json
{
  "tier_policies": {
    "free": {"priority": 10, "soft_quota_pct": 0.6, "grace_tokens": 200},
    "pro": {"priority": 30, "soft_quota_pct": 0.85, "grace_tokens": 2000},
    "enterprise": {"priority": 60, "soft_quota_pct": 0.95, "grace_tokens": 20000}
  },
  "route_pools": {
    "low_cost_q8": ["m-small-q8"],
    "standard": ["m-medium-q4"],
    "high_perf": ["m-large" ]
  },
  "fallback_matrix": {
    "standard": ["low_cost_q8"],
    "high_perf": ["standard","low_cost_q8"]
  }
}
```
Carole: that looks reasonable. can we add a per-route "max_global_qps" so router can choose alternative when a pool is saturated? also need to ensure model-compatibility checks when falling back (schema, tool-calls).
Alice: yes to both. plan is: router consults policy -> checks pool capacity + tenant quotas -> computes weighted decision graph -> emits decision packet that downstream runtime uses. if incompatible, skip to next fallback and annotate reason (incompatibility).
InfraBot: note: canary deploy rule for router change will run for 10% of tenants in us-west over 24h. monitoring hooks: decision_reason histogram + fallback_rate alert if >1% for pro/enterprise for 1h.
Maria: UI notes — console should display a per-tenant "decision log" with last 100 decisions (searchable) and an aggregated panel: fallback_rate, avg_latency_by_route, token_cost_by-route. also surface top 3 decision_reasons.
Dave: implementation tasks (rough): 1) policy schema + validation; 2) router decision graph engine; 3) runtime hook to accept decision packet; 4) telemetry tagging + ingestion; 5) console panels. estimate 3 sprints if we parallelize.
Ben: edge case: what about multi-region burst where capacity exists but region mismatch causes higher latency — should we prefer cross-region higher cost variant for enterprise always? maybe policy needs region overrides (e.g., enterprise -> prefer home region, allow cross-region if latency within 1.2x).
Alice: good point. add region_preferences with latency_tolerance multiplier.
Carole: enforcement semantics: default behavior = soft-bias; allow tenant flag to opt-in to strict_enforcement (hard) for enterprise customers. needs product sign-off.
Maria: for alerts, add a regression check in Optimize: if fallback_rate_for_any_prompt_set increases by >2x post-deploy, trigger automatic rollback suggestion.
Dave: quick API example for runtime decision packet that runtime consumes:
```text
tenant: t-123
route: m-medium-q4
decision_reason: soft_quota_fallback
fallback_chain: [m-small-q8]
quota_state: soft
telemetry_tags: [tier:pro, region:eu, latency_target:150ms]
```
Alice: next steps: I'll draft a lightweight RFC with schema + sample UI mocks. @Ben @Carole can you review enforcement semantics? @Maria please draft telemetry field list. InfraBot, schedule canary job after RFC approved.
Ben: I can take enforcement semantics. will ping legal on billing implications of grace budget.
Carole: will review and check model-compatibility rules with runtime team.
Maria: will produce telemetry spec and console wireframes.
InfraBot: canary scheduled: 2024-11-05T10:00Z for 24h, percent=10, region=us-west. :white_check_mark:
Alice: thanks all — aim to have RFC by EOD Friday. :rocket:
